title: JSON parameter validation, compatibility shim, and structured error taxonomy for function/tool calls
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Define a canonical JSON Schema format, parameter coercion rules, and an explicit error taxonomy for function/tool calls that covers streaming and non-streaming interactions. Provide a lightweight compatibility shim so older clients and older tool schemas continue to work while we roll out stricter validation in runtime-1.22.

Goals: 1) Unify schema representation used by API, Console, and Runtime so validation is consistent across hosted/dedicated/private deployments. 2) Document permissive vs strict modes, with clear migration steps. 3) Provide structured error objects with stable error codes, human-readable messages, and machine-friendly fields (field_path, expected_type, received_value_preview, suggestion). 4) Ensure streaming responses that include partial validation errors are handled deterministically (error streaming vs immediate abort). 5) Emit telemetry events for validation failures for monitoring and alerting.

Key constraints: - JSON values must be standard JSON types; we will not introduce new types. - Backward compatibility: existing tool schemas that use non-JSON-native annotation (e.g., "@nullable": true) must be supported via the shim. - Validation must be performant: runtime validation should be O(n) over schema size and parameter payload. - Error payloads must be small and safe for logs (truncate long values).

Proposed schema conventions (high level): - Core schema fields: type (string|number|integer|boolean|object|array), properties (map of name->schema), required (list), items (schema), enum, default, format (email, uri, date-time), deprecated (boolean as string), description. - Custom Redwood extensions (prefixed with "x-rw-") allowed for console display hints only, not for validation semantics. - Deprecated legacy annotations supported by shim: "@nullable" -> allowed in permissive mode, coerced to {"type": ["null", ...]}.

Validation modes: - permissive: coerce strings to numbers when safe, accept missing optional fields, convert single-value to single-item array if schema expects array and payload is non-array. Log a validation warning. - strict: reject type mismatches and missing required fields with canonical error codes. Default for runtime-1.22 is permissive for a 6-week migration window, then strict for new projects.

Parameter coercion rules (permissive): - numeric strings -> numbers if JSON.parse yields same numeric value. - "true"/"false" strings -> boolean. - single scalar to single-element array if schema items present. - nulls: only allowed when schema includes "null" type.

Error taxonomy (canonical): - RW_VAL_001 MissingRequiredField: required field missing. fields: [field_path]. HTTP: 400. - RW_VAL_002 TypeMismatch: type mismatch detected and cannot be coerced. fields: [field_path], expected_type, received_type. HTTP: 400. - RW_VAL_003 CoercionApplied: coercion applied successfully (warning). fields: [field_path], coercion_details. HTTP: 200 with warning header. - RW_VAL_004 EnumMismatch: value not in enum. fields: [field_path]. HTTP: 400. - RW_VAL_005 SchemaParseError: tool schema invalid/unsupported. HTTP: 422. - RW_VAL_006 StreamingPartialFailure: partial validation failure detected during streaming response; stream includes a terminal error event. HTTP: 206/streaming error envelope.

Error payload shape (must be flat JSON for downstream): - code: RW_VAL_xxx (string) - message: short human message (string) - field_path: dot.notation[] (list of strings) - expected: short string summary (string) - received_preview: short string (string) - suggestion: short string (string) Example (as returned): { code: "RW_VAL_002", message: "type mismatch for 'params.user_id'", field_path: ["params","user_id"], expected: "integer", received_preview: \"42abc\", suggestion: "send an integer or use permissive mode." }

Streaming considerations: - Validation must run incrementally for streaming calls that supply parameters followed by tokens. If param validation fails pre-tokenization, return an immediate terminal validation error and do not start token generation. - If validation detects an error mid-stream (e.g., callback payload shape violated by tool-returned data), emit RW_VAL_006 with a stable finalization envelope and, depending on policy, either continue with fallback model or abort. - Streaming error envelope format must be small and safe for clients; include error.code and error.message.

Telemetry & observability: - Emit event "validation.failure" with tags: code, project, model_variant, client_version, environment (hosted/dedicated/private). - Emit "validation.coercion" for permissive-mode coercions. - Add Console view for top N validation codes by route and customer.

Migration and rollout plan: 1) Implement shim in runtime that translates legacy annotations into canonical schema (2 weeks). 2) Add validation library used by Console and SDKs to surface warnings (2 weeks). 3) Enable permissive-mode validation by default and add a project flag to opt-in to strict (4 weeks). 4) After 6 weeks, evaluate telemetry and flip new projects to strict by default; provide a 30-day deprecation notice for legacy annotations (6 weeks + 30 days).

Acceptance criteria: - Runtime returns canonical error codes and payloads per taxonomy. - Console shows validation warning telemetry and links to offending requests/parameter previews. - Backward compatibility shim converts legacy annotations for 95% of current in-the-wild tool schemas. - Documentation and SDK changes published with examples and migration guide.

Open questions: - Should coercion be opt-in per project or per route? Recommend per-project flag with per-route override. - How to represent deeply nested field_path for arrays in a compact way? Propose dot and index notation (params.items[3].id).

Implementation notes: - Reference parsing library: ajv (Node) for schema validation, custom lightweight validator in runtime C++/Rust for low-latency checks. - GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7456 (draft). - Console story: link to internal doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/FUNC/Validation+v2+RFC (draft).
comments: 2026-02-21 - Diego Morales: Kickoff sync done. Agreed to reuse AJV for SDK/server-side validation but runtime needs a native validator. Assigned implementation split between runtime team and api-team.
2026-02-26 - Asha Patel: Added initial taxonomy and permissive/strict proposals in description. Asked PM to confirm migration windows.
2026-03-03 - Mei Chen (PM): Migration windows OK. PM requests explicit telemetry fields and an example Console alert rule. Adding to release notes for runtime-1.22.

2026-03-07 - Diego Morales: PoC shim implemented in runtime branch. Performance microbenchmarks show ~1.8% p50 latency increase for small payloads; acceptable. Pushed draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7456.
2026-03-09 - Infra QA: Found edge case where coercion of large numeric strings overflows; added test to reject coercion when magnitude differs by >1e6. Marked as blocker for strict mode flip.
2026-03-10 - Asha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to include 95% conversion target for legacy schemas. Assigned docs and SDK tasks to eng-docs and sdk teams.
